entries.topic: Where Zionism's ideas and organizations began, 1838–1897, and where the first settlers came from

claims.text: Shaftesbury repeatedly lobbied Palmerston to encourage Jewish return; a British consul was appointed in Jerusalem in 1838.
Kalischer lived in Thorn (Toruń), acting rabbi for more than forty years; Derishat Zion published 1862 in Lyck.
Bilu began in Russia in January 1882; Belkind's group in Kharkov was its first base ('Kharkov became the Bilu headquarters'); 14 members reached Jaffa on 6 July 1882; Gederah settled December 1884.
Katowice Conference opened 6 Nov 1884 in Kattowitz (Germany, now Poland); 32 delegates (22 from Russia); chaired by Pinsker; central committee based in Odessa.

First Aliyah: estimates 25,000–60,000; 50–70% later left; Romanian expeditions from Galați, about 600 settled in moshavot including Rosh Pinna and Zichron Ya'akov; a few hundred Jews left Sanaa in 1881–82, arriving about seven months before most Eastern Europeans; Rishon LeZion, Zikhron Ya'akov, Rosh Pinna, Petah Tikva (re-established) 1882.
JVL: nearly 35,000 came in the First Aliyah; almost half left within several years.

entries.topic: Where Jews leaving Eastern Europe went, 1881–1914

claims.text: Posen Library: about 1,700,000 Jews to the US 1881–1914; about 300,000 to England, 100,000 Argentina, 80,000 France, 60,000 Canada, 50,000 South Africa; about 60,000 to Palestine.
My Jewish Learning: more than 2.5 million Jews left Eastern Europe 1881–1914, 'some two million' to the US; 1905–06 from Russia: 3,500 to Palestine.

sources.label: Posen Library of Jewish Culture and Civilization, 'The Mass Migration of Jews', accessed 2026-11-15

entries.topic: Where Jews live today, by country (Jewish Agency / DellaPergola, 2024)

claims.text: JNS, 2 Oct 2024, Jewish Agency data from Sergio DellaPergola: Israel 7.3m, US 6.3m, France 438,500, Canada 400,000, Britain 313,000, Argentina 170,000, Germany 125,000, Russia 123,000, Australia 117,000; 'core' definition.
